litelights.section.storms.haboob.tooltip: Arizona's word for a towering dust storm.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.des: Snaps effects that aren't pixel art by nature onto the 16-per-block texture grid of whatever they land on, so they look like part of Minecraft's own pixels. Fog, bloom and the sky are left smooth. Each effect has its own pixel lock switch on its page: shadows on Shadows, caustics and the water surface on Water, glint and sunbeams on Lighting.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.sha: Sun and mob shadows land in whole texture pixels. Needs Pixel lock on the General page.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.cau: The light pattern under water lands in whole texture pixels. Needs Pixel lock on the General page.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.wat: Waves, the ripple in reflections and the foam edge follow the texture pixels of the water. Needs Pixel lock on the General page.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.gli: Sun glints on blocks and water light whole texture pixels. Needs Pixel lock on the General page.
litelights.option.general.pixel_lock.sun: Where sunbeams touch a block or mob, the lit patch follows its texture pixels. Needs Pixel lock on the General page.
Smooths jagged edges in the world. The HUD and menus are never touched. FXAA is the cheaper one. TAA blends each frame with the last few, so it also calms shimmering on distant detail and thin edges.
litelights.option.general.modded_biome_f: Biomes added by other mods get fog colours that suit them, instead of a plain default.
litelights.option.general.natural_foliag: Grass and leaves get softer, more natural greens in every biome, including those from resource packs and other mods. Colours that aren't green, like autumn orange or pale garden grey, stay as they are.
litelights.option.general.shader_loop_ca: Stops a shader from looping endlessly if the data it's given arrives corrupted, as can happen with some Mac graphics drivers, where it would freeze the game. Each loop stops well past anything a setting asks for, so nothing looks different and nothing gets slower. We do not recommend disabling them. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
We do not recommend disabling them. With the caps off, corrupted data can make a shader loop until the graphics driver gives up and the game freezes.
litelights.toast.reloading_shaders: Reloading resources so the shaders take the change
litelights.option.general.mac.vanilla_te: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it off. On, blocks and block models are drawn with vanilla's own shading, as if LiteLights' block shaders weren't there: no shadows, water effects, weather on glass, glint, LiteLights fog or sway on them, and the switches below do nothing. If a world then loads, the freeze is somewhere in those parts. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_wa: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off leaves LiteLights' water, lava and ice shading out of the block shaders: water looks like vanilla's, with no reflections, large textures, foam, waves or wakes, and lava and ice look plain. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_ca: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off leaves out the rippling light on blocks under water, the waves washing up on beaches, the leaves lying under trees, the puddles in the rain and the snow on leaves and under trees. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_gl: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off leaves out the frost, snow and sand on windows. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_sh: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off leaves sun and mob shadows and LiteLights' light model out of the block shaders: blocks keep vanilla's light, whatever the Shadows page says. Creatures and items keep theirs. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_li: Glow, glint and night tone on blocks

For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off leaves out the enhanced glow of glowing blocks and bloom around them, the glint on water, ice, metal and stone, the night tone and the bright patches where sunbeams land. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_fo: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off, blocks take vanilla's fog (or Sodium's) instead of LiteLights' haze, so the land no longer fades into the sky the same way, and the End's tint is left off them. The sky keeps LiteLights' look. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.general.mac.terrain_sw: For tracking down the freeze on some Macs; players whose game runs should leave it on. Off, plants, leaves, hanging lanterns and hanging signs stand still. This is the only part in the vertex shader; the others are in the pixel shader. A change takes effect with a resource reload, which happens by itself once you close the settings.
litelights.option.sky.palette.descriptio: Vanilla keeps Minecraft's sky colours. Computed works the sky out from the sun's height, with a light tint per biome. Both use the LiteLights sun, moon and stars.
litelights.option.sky.falling_stars.desc: Now and then a star streaks across the night sky.
litelights.option.sky.clouds.description: Flat clouds are one thin layer. Fancy clouds have depth and softer shapes.
litelights.option.sky.cloud_layers.descr: A second layer adds higher, thinner clouds above the first.
litelights.option.fog.look.description: Haze thickens with distance and height and takes on each biome's colour. Vanilla keeps Minecraft's fog.
litelights.option.fog.mist_banks.descrip: Low banks of mist hug the ground, with wisps drifting through. Mist during rain and snow is on the Weather page.
litelights.option.fog.far_terrain.descri: Voxy's and Distant Horizons' far terrain gets LiteLights' haze, mist, storm fog, light and night tone, so it meets the nearby land without a seam.
litelights.option.fog.far_snow.descripti: Far terrain shows Almanac's season: snow where it lies now, none where it has melted, and grass and leaves in the season's colours, even on land the far mod saw in another season. Snow comes and goes in patches as the season turns.
litelights.option.lighting.halo.descript: Bright things glow softly into their surroundings.
litelights.option.lighting.glow_heat.des: Glowing blocks look hotter, and the dark parts of their textures stay dark.
litelights.option.lighting.night_tone.de: Nights turn a cool blue while torches and lava stay warm. It fades out underground.
The air wavers gently over lava, fire, campfires, lit furnaces and magma blocks, and over deserts and badlands at midday in clear weather. Strongest just above the heat, and gone past about 48 blocks.
litelights.option.lighting.sunbeams.desc: Sunbeams through the air, through leaves and past the edges of hills.
litelights.option.lighting.underwater_su: Shafts of light reach down from the surface when you're under water.
How bright the underwater shafts are.
litelights.option.lighting.sunbeam_quali: How finely sunbeams are drawn, in air and under water. Low draws them at a quarter of the screen's resolution, Medium at half, High at full, and Ultra at full with twice the slices for smoother long beams.
litelights.option.lighting.submerged_gli: Seen from under water, the surface and the blocks below sparkle where sunlight comes through.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_water_s: How the sun's sparkles on water look. Lower gives small, sharp sparkles scattered over the water; higher gathers them into a wider, softer sheen around the sun's reflection. Also used for glint under water. 50% is the default.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_water_i: How bright the glint on water is, and the glint under water. 50% is the default, 100% twice as bright, 0% none.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_ground_: How the glints on ice and snow, metal and glass, sand and stone, and ores and crystals look. 50%, the default, gives small, sharp sparkles; lower makes them rarer and crisper (and tinier, with Pixel-locked glint off); higher spreads them into a soft sheen.
How bright the glint on ice and snow, metal and glass, sand and stone, and ores and crystals is. 50% is the default, 100% twice as bright, 0% none.
Changes the colours of the whole picture. Choose one grade for all day, or a grade each for dawn, midday, dusk and night that blend as the sun moves.
litelights.grading.editing.description: Which time of day the sliders below change. Use the preview buttons at the bottom to see it.
Brightens or darkens everything, in camera stops.
Pushes darks and lights apart, or draws them together.
litelights.option.colour_grade.shadows.d: Lifts or deepens the darkest parts of the picture.
Lifts or lowers the middle of the range.
litelights.option.colour_grade.highlight: Brightens or tames the brightest parts.
litelights.option.colour_grade.saturatio: Makes every colour stronger or weaker.
Strengthens dull colours more than ones that are already strong.
litelights.option.colour_grade.hue_shift: Turns every colour around the colour wheel.
litelights.option.colour_grade.temperatu: Warmer towards orange, cooler towards blue.
litelights.option.colour_grade.red_stren: How much red there is in the picture.
litelights.option.colour_grade.green_str: How much green there is in the picture.
litelights.option.colour_grade.blue_stre: How much blue there is in the picture.
litelights.option.colour_grade.red_hue.d: Turns reds towards orange or towards pink.
litelights.option.colour_grade.green_hue: Turns greens towards yellow or towards teal.
Turns blues towards cyan or towards purple.
The sun and moon cast real shadows from blocks, plants and mobs.
litelights.option.shadows.light_model.de: Relit also relights the world from the sun, with warm direct light and cooler shade. Shadows only keeps vanilla's light and adds the shadows.
litelights.option.shadows.sun_brightness: Deepens shadows beyond Darkness. At 0 % shadows keep their usual look; at 100 % a shadow in full sun is nearly black. Torches, lanterns and held lights keep their full strength inside shadows.
litelights.option.shadows.sunlight_colou: How much colour the sunlight carries, deepest at sunrise and sunset.
litelights.option.shadows.reach.descript: How far away shadows are still drawn. Further costs more.
litelights.option.shadows.detail.descrip: The size of the sun's shadow map: Fastest 1024, Fast 2048, Sharp 3072, Sharpest 4096, Ultra 8192 pixels a side. Sharper edges cost more video memory and redraw time: about 12 MB at Fastest, 145 MB at Sharpest and 530 MB at Ultra, which is for graphics cards with plenty to spare. If the card can't hold the chosen size, LiteLights uses the next one down and says so here.
litelights.option.shadows.offset.descrip: To keep a surface from shading itself, each point checks for shadow from a spot moved slightly off the surface. A smaller move keeps the shadows of small things right at the ground, such as grass and flower stems, but can leave speckles on slopes and stairs when the sun is low. A bigger move cleans those up but steps over the smallest shadows. Balanced is the usual look.
litelights.option.shadows.glide.descript: Shadows glide as the sun moves instead of stepping.
litelights.shadows.calculate_distance.de: Sets Reach to your render distance, %s chunks, which is %s blocks. That is where Voxy's or Distant Horizons' terrain begins, so the sharp shadows nearby fade into the far terrain's shadows right there and the two read as one set of shadows. With a longer Reach, a ring of far terrain just past the loaded land gets no shadows at all; with a shorter one, the sharp shadows end before the loaded land does. Press it again after changing the render distance. Reach goes from 64 to 512 blocks, so past 32 chunks it stops at 512.
litelights.option.shadows.entities.descr: Mobs, and your own body, cast shadows from the sun.
litelights.option.shadows.in_water.descr: Shadows carry on below the water surface.
litelights.option.shadows.far.descriptio: Shadows past the shadow distance, on far land and on Voxy's and Distant Horizons' terrain. Screen space finds hills that are on screen. Advanced also finds ones that aren't, such as a mountain behind you, from a map of the loaded land's heights: it costs much more, and about 8 MB of video memory.
litelights.option.water.palette.descript: Enhanced keeps the water texture's pixels, resource packs' included, with Natural's colour, depth and light. Natural gives water clearer shallows and deeper blues and greens.
litelights.option.water.biome_depth_colo: Water takes its biome's colour and darkens as it gets deeper.
litelights.option.water.mirrors.descript: Water reflects the sky and the world around it.
litelights.option.water.ice_mirrors.desc: Ice reflects the sky and the world too.
litelights.option.water.mirror_detail.de: Finer detail finds more of the world in reflections, at more cost.
litelights.option.water.edge_foam.descri: A line of foam where water meets land.
litelights.option.water.edge_foam_blocks: Edge foam lines the water only where it meets a block: a shore, a wall, an island. Off, it also lines the edges of thin flowing water where it simply runs out on flat ground, such as a spring spreading over the grass or the fringe of a pool.
litelights.option.water.foam_motion.desc: Stationary: foam stays where it forms. Drifting: on flowing water, such as streams, rapids and the water below a waterfall, the foam slowly travels downstream with the current, faster where the water runs faster. Foam on still water, such as lakes and the sea, stays where it is.
litelights.option.water.ocean_waves.desc: Long, gentle swell rolls across the sea with the wind. Near the shore the waves turn to come straight in, sharpen, break into foam and run a little way up the beach before sliding back, leaving the sand wet for a moment. They grow stronger and faster in rain and thunderstorms and calm down on a still morning. Only on oceans and other large open water: ponds and rivers stay calm.
litelights.option.water.shore_run_up.des: How far the waves run up the beach after they break, on a fair day: 1 block is the usual run-up, 2 blocks twice as far. Rough seas run further whatever this is set to, up to about three blocks in a thunderstorm. The water never runs over a wall or up a step.
litelights.option.water.shore_film.descr: How the water the waves run up the beach looks. Water: a thin, clear sheet of sea water, up and back. Foam: foam all the way up and all the way back, thinning as it drains. Foam in, water out: foam as it runs up the sand, turning into clear water as it slides back.
litelights.option.water.wave_foam.descri: How thick the ocean waves' foam is: the breaking crests, the band of surf and the foam on the water running up the beach. Below 100% the lines are thinner with less lace, above it thicker. Edge foam and the foam on wakes aren't changed.
litelights.option.water.caustics.descrip: Rippling light patterns on blocks under water.
Leaves drift on water near trees. Leaves on the ground under trees have their own switch on the Vegetation page.
litelights.option.water.lava_crust.descr: Lava pools grow a dark, cooling crust that cracks and glows.
Things far away under water go soft.
litelights.option.water.large_textures.d: Water and lava textures stretch over several blocks instead of repeating on every block, so lakes and seas lose the grid.
litelights.option.water.large_textures.c: Idea and vanilla-style textures by Tec (Big Water)
litelights.option.water.large_water_scal: How many blocks one water texture covers.
litelights.option.water.large_lava_scale: How many blocks one lava texture covers.
litelights.option.water.far_terrain.desc: Water on Voxy's and Distant Horizons' far terrain reflects the sky and the sun, at any height, lakes and rivers too. It is found by what the far mod draws over the ground, so far stained glass or ice can count as water.
litelights.option.water.far_caustics.des: Rippling sunlight on the bottom of shallow far water, fading out where it would be smaller than a pixel. Needs Voxy or Distant Horizons.
litelights.option.water.far_depth_colour: Far water darkens and takes on its tint as it gets deeper, like the water nearby. Needs Voxy or Distant Horizons.
litelights.option.water.far_edge_foam.de: A thin line of foam where far water meets its shore. Needs Voxy or Distant Horizons.
litelights.option.water.jump_splash.desc: Falling or jumping into water makes a splash; bigger falls make bigger splashes. Basic: droplets, a ring of foam and ripples. Advanced: a pixel-style square ring spreading from where you land and water thrown up.
litelights.option.water.wakes.descriptio: Boats and swimmers leave wakes behind them: ripples that spread in a V, cross each other, bounce off the shore and fade, with foam along the trail. Things falling into water send out rings, and a fast boat throws spray from its bow. Drawn within about 30 blocks of you.
litelights.option.water.wake_strength.de: How big the wakes and rings are.
litelights.option.water.wake_foam.descri: White foam along a wake's trail and on the crests it throws up.
Grass, tall grass and ferns move in the wind. Their roots stay put, and the wind blows a little harder in rain and storms.
litelights.option.vegetation.sway_plants: Flowers, saplings, crops and similar plants move in the wind. Flat, hanging and bushy plants stay still.
litelights.option.vegetation.sway_leaves: Tree leaves shimmer gently in the wind, without opening gaps in the canopy.
litelights.option.vegetation.sway_lanter: Hanging lanterns swing gently in the wind, and harder and gustier in rain and thunderstorms. A lantern on a chain swings with its whole chain, from the top. Hanging signs swing too, with their text, and so do loose chain ends. Standing lanterns stay put, and the light stays where the lantern hangs.
Swinging lantern idea by Rilith (Swinging Lanterns)
litelights.option.vegetation.ground_leav: Fallen leaves lie scattered on grass, dirt and moss under and around trees, coloured like the leaves above. Ground that already has leaf litter, snow on it or a roof over it is left as it is. Leaves on water have their own switch on the Water page.
litelights.option.particles.density.desc: How many of LiteLights' own particles you see. Off turns them all off, including the Nether's ambience.
litelights.option.particles.snow_sand_sp: Detailed draws falling snow and blowing sand in finer detail.
litelights.option.particles.firefly_swar: Fireflies glow over grass and water on warm nights.
litelights.option.particles.dust.descrip: Specks of dust float in sunbeams and caves.
litelights.option.particles.pollen.descr: Pollen drifts around flowers and meadows.
litelights.option.particles.spores.descr: Spores float near mushrooms and in lush caves.
litelights.option.particles.falling_leav: Leaves drift down from trees and ride the wind: nearly straight down on a calm day, carried sideways and more of them in gusts and storms. Spruce leaves fall too.
Falling leaves idea by Fourmisain (Falling Leaves)
litelights.option.particles.enhanced_fir: Fire gives off lit smoke and embers.
Wood, leaves and other burnable blocks near a fire glow with orange cracks, which fade a few seconds after the fire goes out.
litelights.option.particles.burn_marks.d: Fire leaves soot on the block it burns on, under the flames, which fades slowly after the fire goes out.
litelights.option.particles.enhanced_wat: Falling water runs white, foams where it lands and throws up mist. Higher falls make more.
How rain, snow, storms and blizzards look. Vanilla+ keeps vanilla's rain and snow with a LiteLights layer on top; Enhanced replaces them with LiteLights' own.
litelights.option.weather.density.descri: How many rain drops, snowflakes and grains of blowing sand LiteLights draws. Light is the old amount, Medium twice that. Mist and storm fog only thicken a little; each storm's own Fog density and Cloud particles rows are under Storms. Rain and snow follow it with Enhanced rain and snow; blowing sand always does.
litelights.option.weather.rain_mist.desc: Rain and snow bring a soft mist that closes in the view: a thicker haze, mist along the ground and drifting puffs of mist. Under Storms, each storm's Cloud particles row can leave its puffs out.
litelights.option.weather.mist_style.des: How the drifting puffs of mist, sandstorm dust, Nether ash haze and End mist are drawn. Mist field (the default) draws one rolling layer of mist along with the fog, and stays light even in blizzards. 3D puffs are soft rounded clouds that melt into the ground and walls and look the same from every side; in heavy rain and blizzards they cost the most. Classic billboards are the flat puffs from before 0.9.7, the lightest, if your graphics driver has trouble with the others.
litelights.option.weather.storm_atmosphe: Sandy fog in dry biomes during rain, white-outs in snowy thunderstorms, thick fog in swamps and pale gardens, wind-blown grit in the hills, and dark rain over pale gardens. Each storm's fog and cloud particles are set below.
litelights.option.weather.storms.rain.fo: How thick the grey-blue fog gets in the rain. Light is a thin haze; Normal is thicker, and Dense and Very dense close the view in much further, even up in the hills.
litelights.option.weather.storms.rain.cl: The large, faint puffs of mist that drift low in the rain. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out. Raindrops stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Mist in rain and snow.
litelights.option.weather.storms.thunder: How thick the fog gets in a thunderstorm: like rain's, a shade darker. Normal is the usual haze; Dense and Very dense close the view in much further. Light thins it.

The puffs of mist that drift low in a thunderstorm. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out. Raindrops stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Mist in rain and snow.
litelights.option.weather.storms.snow.fo: How thick the white fog gets while it snows. Light is a faint whitening; Normal is thicker, and Dense and Very dense close the view in. The white storm fog needs Storm atmosphere.
litelights.option.weather.storms.snow.cl: The white puffs of mist that drift low in snowfall. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out. Snowflakes stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Mist in rain and snow.
litelights.option.weather.storms.blizzar: How thick the white-out gets in a blizzard, a snowy thunderstorm. Normal hides land past about 40 blocks; Very dense is a true white-out. Light thins it. The white-out needs Storm atmosphere.

The big soft clouds of snow that roll through a blizzard. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out and can save some frame time. Snowflakes stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Mist in rain and snow.
litelights.option.weather.storms.sandsto: How thick the sand-coloured fog gets in a sandstorm. Light thins it; Normal hides land past about 60 blocks, and Dense and Very dense close in much further. Needs Sandstorms.

The big soft clouds of dust that roll through a sandstorm. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out and can save some frame time. Grains of sand stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Sandstorms.
How thick the fog gets in a haboob, a sandstorm with thunder: the thickest sandstorm, a shade darker. Dense and Very dense close in much further. Light thins it. Needs Sandstorms.

The big soft clouds of dust that roll through a haboob. Follow density draws them as thick as Weather density says; Off leaves them out and can save some frame time. Grains of sand stay either way, and the fog doesn't change. Needs Sandstorms.
litelights.option.weather.cloud_lightnin: In a thunderstorm, flashes flicker inside the clouds: a patch lit from within, often twice or three times in a row, sometimes spreading across the sky, and far-off ones low on the horizon. Each flash lights the fog and the land a little, and vanilla's bolts light the clouds above them. Everyone on a world sees the same flashes. With Hide Lightning Flashes on (Accessibility), only a faint glow in the clouds is left.
litelights.option.weather.branching_ligh: Vanilla's lightning bolts are drawn as jagged strikes from the clouds to the ground, with forks that thin out and fade, a bright core and a soft glow. They strike in the same place at the same moment as vanilla's. Off draws vanilla's straight bolts.
litelights.option.weather.rain_drips.des: Water drips from wet roof edges, ledges and leaves and splashes where it lands. It keeps dripping for a little while after the rain stops, then tapers off. Works with every Rain and snow setting; needs particles on.
litelights.option.weather.rain_drips.cre: Drip and streak ideas by pigcart (Particle Rain)
litelights.option.weather.wall_streaks.d: Where rain hits a wall of stone, bricks, concrete and the like, or glass and glass panes, short streaks of water run down its face, a little more often on glass. The inside of a window under its roof stays dry. Works with every Rain and snow setting; needs particles on.
litelights.option.weather.wall_streaks.c: Drip and streak ideas by pigcart (Particle Rain)
litelights.option.weather.puddles.descri: Puddles form on open ground in the rain: thin sheets of water on grass, paths, stone, planks and the like, in the colour of your Water colours setting, with rings where the drops land. They grow in over the first couple of minutes, bigger in a thunderstorm, and stay a while after the rain before they shrink and dry up. None under roofs or trees, on sand, snow or farmland, or where it snows.
litelights.option.weather.snowy_leaves.d: In biomes where it snows, leaves open to the sky frost over while it snows: the tops and upper edges first, spruce and other conifers more than oak and birch. The bare grass and dirt under the trees, where vanilla leaves no snow, takes a light, patchy dusting. It builds up over the first couple of minutes of snow, stays half a day after, and thaws slowly during a long dry spell. None under roofs or outside snowy biomes. Snow weather in the settings screen's preview shows it on any trees.
litelights.option.weather.glass.descript: Frost, snow and sand gather along the edges of windows of glass and glass panes, in a band that is wider on larger windows and fuller in the corners. Frost, snow and sand form on the outdoor side (both sides of free-standing glass), and from inside you see them through the glass. Rain on glass comes from Wall streaks. Works with every Rain and snow setting.
litelights.option.weather.glass.credit: Glass weather idea by duffopuffo (Weather Glass)
litelights.option.weather.glass_detail.d: How fine the pixels of frost, snow and dust on glass are: 16x matches vanilla's 16 pixels to a block, 32x is twice as fine.
litelights.option.weather.glass_frost.de: Where it is cold enough to snow, frost grows in from the edges of each window on its outdoor side, corners first. In snowfall, snow sticks along the edges outside, deepest along the bottom, and piles higher where there is ground or a ledge below.
litelights.option.weather.glass_dust.des: After a sandstorm, sand settles along the edges of windows outside, a little deeper at the bottom: sand in deserts, red sand in the badlands. Rain washes it off.
Wind carries sand across deserts and badlands.
litelights.option.weather.sandstorms.des: Rain in the desert becomes a sandstorm.
litelights.option.weather.polar_lights.d: Bands of coloured light over cold biomes at night.
Some nights bring a shower of shooting stars.
litelights.option.weather.rainbows.descr: Now and then, when rain or a thunderstorm clears during the day, a rainbow appears opposite the sun for a few minutes, with a fainter second bow outside it. Best in the morning and evening: with the sun high, most of the bow is below the horizon. Everyone on the world sees the same one.
litelights.option.weather.rainbows.credi: Rainbow idea by AppleNButter (You Must Have The Rain)
Some nights, fireworks go off far away on the horizon.
litelights.option.outlines.enabled.descr: Enchanted items held by you, other players and mobs, and enchanted armour being worn, get a soft glowing outline.
litelights.option.outlines.colour.descri: The colour of the outline, the same for every item.
litelights.option.outlines.size.descript: How far the glow spreads from the item.
litelights.option.outlines.saturation.de: How strong the glow's colour is.
litelights.option.outlines.diffusion.des: How soft the outline is: 0% is a crisp, solid line, 50% the usual soft glow, 100% twice as soft.
litelights.option.outlines.worn_armour.d: Enchanted armour worn by you (seen from outside), other players and mobs gets the outline too, up to 64 blocks away.
Hides the game's moving enchantment shimmer on the items and armour that get an outline, so only the outline shows they are enchanted. Enchanted items that get no outline (dropped, in item frames, in the inventory, or too far away) keep their shimmer.
Enchanted armour with a trim glows in the trim material's colour instead of the glow colour, piece by piece. Untrimmed armour and weapons keep the glow colour.
litelights.option.dimensions.end.haze.de: A dark haze fills the distance in the End.
litelights.option.dimensions.end.sky_glo: A faint glow moves across the End sky.
litelights.option.dimensions.end.tint.de: Gives the End a purple tint.
litelights.option.dimensions.end.motes.d: Motes drift through the air in the End.
LiteLights' sky, sun, moon and stars in this dimension.

litelights.compat.facing_fix.description: Sodium 0.9.2 sometimes files Continuity's overlays under the wrong side of a block, so its block face culling hides them at some distances and angles. This files each overlay under the side it's drawn on. Nothing extra is drawn. It runs by itself whenever Sodium 0.9.2 and Continuity are both installed; there is nothing to set.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.tag.tooltip: This is a fix for a current bug between Continuity and Sodium, and will be removed once the fix is implemented in either of those mods.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.no_sodium: Sodium isn't installed, and this only fixes a bug in Sodium.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.no_continui: Continuity isn't installed, so there are no overlays for Sodium to hide.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.fixed_in_so: This Sodium version already files overlays under the right side.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.unknown_sod: This Sodium version is built differently from the one the fix is for, so the fix stays out. The log says more.
litelights.compat.facing_fix.failed: The fix hit an error and turned itself off until the game restarts. The log says more.
litelights.compat.wakes_fix.description: Wakes draws its wakes without what Improved Transparency needs, which crashes the game with Improved Transparency on, with or without LiteLights. LiteLights draws them after the rest of the transparent world instead, as they would be drawn with Improved Transparency off. With it off, nothing changes. It runs by itself whenever Wakes is installed; there is nothing to set.
litelights.compat.wakes_fix.tag.tooltip: This is a fix for a current bug between Wakes and Improved Transparency, and will be removed once the fix is implemented in Wakes.
litelights.compat.wakes_fix.failed: The fix hit an error and turned itself off until the game restarts, so with Improved Transparency on the wakes stay hidden. The log says more.
litelights.shadows.detail_too_large: This graphics card can't make a shadow map that large, so a smaller detail is in use.
litelights.shadows.detail_no_memory: Not enough video memory for this shadow detail, so a smaller one is in use. Retry tries the chosen detail again.

litelights.about.summary: LiteLights adds shadows, water, sky, fog and ambient effects that keep Minecraft's own look, and stays fast.
litelights.about.credits.description: Every project LiteLights took ideas or textures from, with its author and a link.
litelights.about.group.recommended.descr: Mods that make LiteLights better. Not one of them is required.
litelights.about.group.works_with.descri: Tested together. Where two mods could draw the same thing, one of them steps aside.
litelights.about.group.not_compatible.de: LiteLights can't run beside these, or turns a part of itself off for them.
litelights.about.mod.sodium: Faster chunk rendering. LiteLights shades Sodium's terrain through its shaders and adds its pages to Sodium's Video Settings.
litelights.about.mod.lambdynamiclights: Light from held and moving items, which every LiteLights light model picks up.
litelights.about.mod.lambdabettergrass: Grass and snow over block sides. The overlays module leaves it the faces it redraws.
litelights.about.mod.continuity: Draws the overlays module's overlays. Without it the module stays off.
litelights.about.mod.visuality: Small particles of its own (crystal sparkles, slime blobs and more), alongside LiteLights' particles.
litelights.about.mod.subtle_effects: Many subtle particle details and a few sounds of its own, alongside LiteLights' effects.
litelights.about.mod.modmenu: Opens LiteLights' settings from the mod list.
litelights.about.mod.voxy: Far terrain gets LiteLights' haze, light, far shadows and far water. OpenGL only.
litelights.about.mod.distanthorizons: Far terrain gets LiteLights' haze, light, far shadows and far water; its own fog steps aside.
litelights.about.mod.particle_rain: Handles rain, snow and sandstorm particles; LiteLights' own step aside. Fog, mist and sky stay.
litelights.about.mod.immersive_storms: Handles sandstorms, storm fog and wind-blown dust; LiteLights' versions step aside.
litelights.about.mod.wakes: Draws its own wakes and splashes; LiteLights' wakes step aside, and of its splashes only the player's jump splash stays.
litelights.about.mod.weather_glass: Handles rain, frost, snow, dust and breath on glass; LiteLights' weather on glass steps aside.
litelights.about.mod.big_water: Handles large water and lava textures; LiteLights' own turn off. Needs Sodium stable: Big Water 1.2.0 doesn't run on Sodium 0.9.3-beta.5.
litelights.about.mod.punchy: First-person animations and hands. Enchantment outlines follow the items it animates in first person.
litelights.about.mod.sodium_extra: More of Sodium's options. Works alongside.
litelights.about.mod.reeses_sodium_optio: Restyles Sodium's Video Settings, LiteLights' pages included.
litelights.about.mod.scalablelux: A faster light engine. Its light still reaches LiteLights' shaders and LambDynamicLights.
litelights.about.mod.better_block_entiti: Chests, signs and beds drawn as blocks get LiteLights' shading and cast shadows.
litelights.about.mod.iris: Shader packs replace the same rendering, so LiteLights refuses to load beside Iris.
litelights.about.mod.dynamic_overlays: The standalone version of the overlays module. With it installed, the module stays off.
litelights.about.reset_all.description: Puts every LiteLights setting back to its default. Click twice to confirm.
litelights.credits.intro: LiteLights is written from scratch. These projects gave it ideas, textures or code, or work alongside it. Links open in your browser after Minecraft asks.
litelights.credits.immersivevfx.used: Ideas: the cached shadow map, forward-shaded effects and biome atmosphere.
litelights.credits.realistic_biomes.used: Inspiration: the atmosphere effects that inspired ImmersiveVFX's.
litelights.credits.big_water.used: Idea and textures: water and lava textures that span several blocks, and its vanilla-style water and lava textures (CC0-1.0).
litelights.credits.immersive_storms.used: Ideas: the storm atmosphere (sandstorm fog, blizzards, swamp and pale garden fog, ambient wind, dark pale-garden rain).
litelights.credits.squall.used: Idea: lightning flickering inside the clouds, lighting them and the land.
litelights.credits.tempestra.used: Idea: branching lightning bolts instead of straight ones.
litelights.credits.weather_glass.used: Idea: weather on glass (frost, stuck snow, dust after sandstorms).
litelights.credits.particle_rain.used: Ideas: rain drips from eaves, ledges and leaves, and water streaks on walls. It also works alongside LiteLights.
litelights.credits.wakes.used: Idea: wakes behind boats and swimmers, and rings where things fall into water. It also works alongside LiteLights.
litelights.credits.falling_leaves.used: Idea: leaves falling from every kind of tree and drifting on the wind. If it is installed, LiteLights leaves falling leaves to it.
litelights.credits.you_must_have_the_rai: Idea: rainbows after rain and thunderstorms.
litelights.credits.snow.used: Idea: leaves turning white while it snows, and snow under trees.
litelights.credits.swinging_lanterns.use: Idea: hanging lanterns and their chains swinging in the wind, harder in rain and thunder.
litelights.credits.lava_particles_more.u: Idea: the heat shimmer over lava, fire and hot ground, from its heat waves over lava geysers.
litelights.credits.lambdynamiclights.use: Recommended companion: light from held and dropped items.
litelights.credits.lambdabettergrass.use: Recommended companion: grass and snow that cover block sides.
litelights.credits.subtle_effects.used: Recommended companion: many more subtle particle details.

litelights.overlays.pack.title: LiteLights overlays
litelights.overlays.pack.description: Overlays built from your packs. Turn off in LiteLights settings.
litelights.overlays.off.standalone_insta: Off: the Dynamic Overlays mod is installed on its own and draws these overlays already. Remove it to use this module; its settings are imported the first time LiteLights runs without it.
litelights.overlays.drawing.in_use: Right now: drawn by Continuity through the module's own method, with edge variety and steps.
litelights.overlays.drawing.chosen_plain: Right now: plain overlays, because "Plain overlays only" is on.
litelights.overlays.drawing.fallback: Right now: plain overlays, because the module's own Continuity method couldn't be used (%s). Everything else still works; the log has the details.
litelights.overlays.caption.grass_and_sa: Grass and sand in one group
litelights.overlays.caption.skipped: Left out of the last build (%s)
litelights.overlays.note.blocks: Softer blocks spill onto harder ones. Pick a style for each block here, or open the hierarchy to change the order, add blocks or remove them.
litelights.overlays.note.export: Saves the current overlays as an ordinary resource pack in your resource packs folder, to share or to use without LiteLights. Continuity still draws them, with its plain overlay method: other players won't have the module's own method, so an export has no edge variety and doesn't spill down steps. While the overlays are on, leave the exported pack off: it won't follow later changes, and any pair it covers is left to it.
litelights.overlays.note.how_it_works: Each time resource packs load, LiteLights cuts edge tiles from the textures of your current packs and hands them to Continuity, which draws them. Nothing is written to disk. If one of your packs already has an overlay for a pair of blocks, that pair is left to the pack.
litelights.overlays.note.when_rebuilt: Overlays are textures, so they change with a resource reload. That happens by itself when you change packs or press F3+T, and once when you close these settings after changing anything that affects them. Rebuild now does it straight away.
litelights.overlays.note.texture_sizes: Overlays are made at the size of the texture they come from, from 4x up, power of two or not, so a 128x pack gets 128x edges. Textures above Largest overlay size (512x unless you change it) are drawn at that size. Bigger textures also get finer detail along their edges, so a 128x edge has 128x pixels. If a pack's overlays would make the block atlas grow too much, and the reload with it, edge variety steps down, as far as off; a 128x pack normally gets Low. Only if even that wouldn't fit a safe atlas size are the largest textures drawn smaller. Any such step is listed under About the last build. Animated textures give their first frame. A texture that isn't square is left out and listed below.
litelights.overlays.note.variety_help: In a long straight border every block used to get the same edge, so the border repeated once per block. Now each block corner gets one of a few depths and each edge one of a few wave shapes, picked from its position in the world, so neighbours always meet cleanly but the pattern doesn't repeat. Low, Normal and High make more variants; each step costs a little more texture memory.
litelights.overlays.note.other_mods: With LambdaBetterGrass installed, every side face it redraws is its own: where it turns a grass, mycelium, podzol, nylium or path side into its connected grass, its blended edges or a snowy side, that face shows only its work. Each face is decided by what it actually drew, so its mode and the blocks around follow automatically. Nothing else changes: those blocks still spill onto their neighbours exactly as without it, and sides it leaves looking like vanilla keep their overlays, and so do tops and steps. Water never takes part: it can't be added to the hierarchy, and blocks under water or beside waterlogged blocks get their overlays as on dry land.
litelights.overlays.note.steps_help: Where a softer block sits one step above a harder one, the face of the step spills a little onto the lower block's top, as if soil and debris had crumbled down. This only happens on full blocks; slabs and stairs are never touched.
litelights.overlays.note.grass_and_sand: By default grass and sand are in different groups, so grass covers sand. To make them interlock instead, put them in one group: in the hierarchy editor, select Sand and press Softer group, or select Ground cover and press Merge with next. Then turn on Blend within a group. Every pair of blocks in that group interlocks the same way.
litelights.overlays.setting.enabled.desc: Draw soft edges where softer blocks meet harder ones. Off leaves every block as your packs draw it.
litelights.overlays.setting.fallback_sty: The edge shape for every block set to Default. Organic wanders like turf, Jagged steps like pixel-art grass, Clean is a solid rim with a short pixel dither just past it, Clumps grows round tufts out of a thin band and Dithered fades out in a pixel pattern. Bricks needs a brick texture, so it's chosen per block, not here.
litelights.overlays.setting.force_fallba: Use the fallback for every block
Ignore each block's own style and use the fallback everywhere. The per-block choices stay saved for when you turn this off.
litelights.overlays.setting.edge_reach.d: How far an edge reaches onto the harder block, in sixteenths of a block. At 16x that's one pixel per step; 8x and 32x packs scale to match.
litelights.overlays.setting.edge_roughne: How much the edge wanders around its reach. Low is calm and even, high is wild.
litelights.overlays.setting.edge_variety: How many variants of each edge are made, so long straight borders don't repeat once per block. Off makes one, like a plain overlay pack. More variety costs a little more texture memory.
litelights.overlays.setting.spill_down_s: Where a softer block stands one step above a harder one, its face spills a little onto the lower block's top.
litelights.overlays.setting.plain_overla: Draw with Continuity's own overlay method, as an exported pack does: no edge variety and no spilling down steps. For comparing, or if something about the variety looks wrong.
litelights.overlays.setting.largest_over: Textures larger than this are drawn at this size. Overlays are only ever made at the size of the textures you're using, so a high limit costs nothing until a pack that large is on. Lower it if a 256x or 512x pack makes reloads too slow.
litelights.overlays.setting.blend_within: Where two blocks of the same group touch, both spill a little so their edges interlock, instead of the softer one covering the harder. Blocks in different groups always go softer onto harder. To blend grass and sand, put them in one group first (see Help).
litelights.overlays.setting.rebuild.desc: Save these settings and reload resource packs so the overlays rebuild straight away.
litelights.overlays.setting.edit_hierarc: Change the order of groups and blocks, make or merge groups, and add or remove blocks.
Write the overlays your current packs give into a zip in your resource packs folder. Exports use plain overlays, without edge variety or steps.
Open the folder exported packs go into.
litelights.overlays.status.none: No overlays built yet in this session.
litelights.overlays.status.built: %s overlay sets from %s blocks, built in %s ms with %s. %s left out (see Help).
litelights.overlays.block.description: %s. Off leaves the block out entirely. Receive only takes overlays from softer blocks but never spills its own. Bricks, for brick and tile blocks, reaches into its neighbours with whole bricks cut along the texture's own mortar lines, and merges both ways with the other Bricks blocks of its group.
litelights.overlays.editor.title: Hardness hierarchy
litelights.overlays.editor.subtitle: Softest first: each block spills onto every block below it
litelights.overlays.editor.flow: Takes overlays from %s blocks and spills onto or blends with %s.
litelights.overlays.editor.cannot_spill: You sink into this block, so it can't spill its own overlay. It can still receive them.
litelights.overlays.editor.group_help: Merge keeps every block. Delete removes the group and its blocks. With blending on, blocks in one group interlock instead of overlapping, so merging Ground cover with Sand makes grass and sand interlock.
litelights.overlays.editor.keys: Drag blocks to move them. Shift with Up or Down moves the selection.
litelights.overlays.picker.title: Add blocks
litelights.overlays.status.cost: Generation took %s ms on a background thread and allocated %s MiB.
litelights.overlays.off.no_continuity: Off: overlays need Continuity. Install it to use them.
litelights.about.mod.streams_reflowing: Its streams, lakes and waterfalls are plain water, so every water effect works on them. While its own waterfall spray is on, LiteLights' waterfall particles step aside; the white falling water and the foam where it lands stay.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_water.d: The sun sparkles on water. The sparkles shift as you move; far away they become a soft sheen around the sun's reflection.
litelights.option.lighting.water_sparkle: Still: sparkles only shift as you move. Gentle: they also drift slowly with the waves, each fading in and out. Lively: the waves move them faster.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_ice_sno: Ice and snow catch the sun on the faces turned toward it.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_metal_g: Metal blocks, lanterns, chains and glass catch the sun on the faces turned toward it.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_sand_st: A rare, tiny glimmer on sand and stone, only with the sun low and only on faces it lights. Ores and crystals have a row of their own.
litelights.option.lighting.glint_ores.de: The ore in ore blocks twinkles in its own colour, even in the dark and from most angles, so ores are easier to spot underground; the rock around it stays as it is. Amethyst, diamond and emerald blocks sparkle too. Only on faces you can see, and it fades out between about 24 and 48 blocks.
litelights.option.lighting.ore_sparkle.d: Still: sparkles shift only as you move, and slowly; now and then one flares by itself. Gentle: they twinkle slowly by themselves, whether or not you move.
litelights.preview.weather.thunder_sands: Arizona's word for a towering dust storm.
litelights.preview.time.tooltip:
Time of day preview: %s. Click for %s.

Shows LiteLights' sky, light and grade as at that time. Your world's time doesn't change.
litelights.preview.weather.tooltip:
Weather preview: %s. Click for %s.

Shows LiteLights' fog, storms, sky, sunbeams and its own rain, snow and sand as in that weather, whatever the biome. Your world's weather doesn't change and no real rain or sound starts.
litelights.preview.event.tooltip:
Sky event preview: %s. Click for %s.

Shows the event tonight, anywhere, in the part of the sky you're looking at, and previews the night with it (a rainbow shows by day instead). Your world doesn't change.
litelights.preview.switched_off: %s is switched off, so there is nothing to see. Switch it on to preview it.
litelights.getting_started.summary: LiteLights adds shadows, light, sky, fog, water and weather to Minecraft's own look, without a shader pack. Every change shows on the world behind this panel as you make it.
litelights.getting_started.sodium: Sodium: much faster rendering. LiteLights' pages appear in its Video Settings too.
litelights.getting_started.lambdynamicli: LambDynamicLights: torches and lanterns you hold light up the world.
litelights.getting_started.lambdabetterg: LambdaBetterGrass: grass and snow spread over the sides of blocks.
litelights.getting_started.continuity: Continuity: draws the soft block edges the Overlays page makes.
litelights.getting_started.visuality: Visuality: more small particles, like sparkles on crystals.
litelights.getting_started.subtle_effect: Subtle Effects: many more little details, like dust trickling from sand.
litelights.getting_started.tip.gpu: Tip: on a weaker graphics card, lower Detail on the Shadows page and Sunbeam quality on the Lighting page first.
litelights.getting_started.tip.far_terra: Tip: Far terrain turns on by itself when Voxy or Distant Horizons is installed.
litelights.setup.title: How powerful is your computer?
litelights.setup.subtitle: LiteLights will pick its settings to suit it. You can change any of them later in LiteLights' settings.
litelights.setup.point: Point at an answer to see who it's for.
litelights.setup.hint: Not sure? The creator's recommended is a safe middle.
litelights.setup.tier.integrated.descrip: For an aging computer, or a laptop that isn't particularly powerful, that you'd like Minecraft to look a bit nicer on. Every effect stays, at its lightest.
litelights.setup.tier.integrated.cpu: CPU: 8th Gen Intel Core i3 or older
litelights.setup.tier.integrated.gpu: GPU: Integrated graphics or an outdated video card
litelights.setup.tier.everyday.descripti: For a newer everyday computer or laptop, bought for work, school or browsing rather than for games.
litelights.setup.tier.everyday.cpu: CPU: A recent Core i5, Ryzen 5 or similar
litelights.setup.tier.everyday.gpu: GPU: The graphics built into a recent processor (such as Intel Iris Xe or Arc, or AMD Radeon 780M), or a basic video card
litelights.setup.tier.gaming.description: For a gaming computer that's a few years old, or a budget one, that runs most games but not on their highest settings.
litelights.setup.tier.gaming.cpu: CPU: A Core i5 or Ryzen 5 from the last several years
litelights.setup.tier.gaming.gpu: GPU: About a GTX 1060 to RTX 3060, or an RX 580 to RX 6600
litelights.setup.tier.top: Top of the line gaming PC
litelights.setup.tier.top.description: For a powerful, recent gaming computer that plays new games on high settings. Nearly everything is turned up as far as it goes.
litelights.setup.tier.top.cpu: CPU: A recent Core i7, Ryzen 7 or better
litelights.setup.tier.top.gpu: GPU: A Radeon RX 9070 XT, GeForce RTX 5070 Ti or RTX 4080, or better
litelights.setup.recommended.description: LiteLights the way its creator set it up: a good look at a fair cost, in between the two middle answers. A safe choice if you're not sure.
litelights.setup.again.description: Asks again how powerful your computer is, as LiteLights did the first time. Each answer sets the quality and distance settings to suit; the creator's recommended puts those back to their defaults. Colours and other looks stay as you set them.
litelights.getting_started.tip.preview: Tip: the preview buttons at the bottom only change what you see here, never your world's time or weather.
litelights.option.colour_grade.tone_curv: The curve the finished picture goes through. Vanilla-friendly keeps the picture as it is and only softens what the grade pushes past white. ACES-style gives deeper shadows and richer highlights, AgX-style gentle contrast with bright colours turning toward white, Hable filmic lifted shadows and a soft, film-like top end. Works with grading off too.
litelights.grading.template.description: Fills the sliders below with a ready-made look in one click: all four times of day when grading goes by time of day, the whole-day set otherwise. It isn't a mode: every slider stays free to change, and this row shows Your own once they differ.
litelights.option.fog.biome_haze_tint.de: How much each biome colours its haze, such as the desert's orange or the swamp's green. At 0 % every biome has the same neutral haze; 100 % is each biome's own colour.
litelights.option.fog.sun_glow.descripti: At sunrise and sunset: the warm glow in the haze toward a low sun, and the haze's warming around sunrise and sunset. 0 % leaves the haze its daytime colour; 100 % is the built-in look.
litelights.option.particles.distance.des: How far around you fireflies, dust specks, pollen and spores reach, and the floating ash, spores and motes of the Nether and the End. Rain, snow and sand have their own distance on the Weather page. Far, Very far and Fill can lower your frame rate.
litelights.option.particles.distance_fil: Spread keeps the same number of fireflies, dust, pollen and spores and spreads them over the wider area: about the same cost, a little thinner close by. Fill keeps them as thick as at Near all the way out, so there are more to draw, which can lower your frame rate. Fireflies keep their number either way. Only matters past Near.
litelights.option.weather.distance.descr: How far around you rain, snow and blowing sand reach. Near is the usual distance; further out, storms show across the land around you. Fireflies, dust and pollen have their own distance on the Particles page. Far, Very far and Fill can lower your frame rate.
Spread keeps the same amount of rain, snow and sand and spreads it over the wider area: about the same cost, a little thinner close by. Fill keeps it as thick as at Near all the way out, so there is more to draw, which can lower your frame rate. Only matters past Near.
